Warm Neutral Canvas Rejecting Pure White

nodes.label: Pinterest Color Palette
nodes.rationale: Warm white canvas with olive/sand-toned neutrals and Pinterest Red (#e60023) as the singular bold brand accent; warmth over cool tech-blue distinguishes Pinterest from other platforms.

nodes.label: Photography-First Masonry Grid
nodes.rationale: Masonry grid packs pins tightly because content density IS the value proposition; whitespace exists between sections, not within the grid. Backed by a three-tier design token architecture (--comp-*/--sema-*/--base-*).

nodes.label: Pin Sans (Custom Typeface)
nodes.rationale: Custom proprietary font with a broad fallback stack including CJK fonts, reflecting Pinterest's global reach; single font family handles all display and UI text.

nodes.label: PostHog Color Palette
nodes.rationale: Warm sage/olive palette instead of conventional SaaS blues, paired with a hidden brand orange (#F54E00) that appears only on hover -- a deliberately anti-corporate, scrappy-startup visual stance.

nodes.label: Hidden Orange Hover Accent
nodes.rationale: PostHog Orange never appears at rest; it flashes on hover across buttons, cards, and links as a deliberate 'delightful surprise' interaction pattern reinforcing the brand's irreverent personality.

nodes.label: IBM Plex Sans Variable
nodes.rationale: Chosen for technical credibility (an IBM developer-context font) deployed at bold weights (700/800) with generous line-heights, balancing serious engineering with playful brand tone.

nodes.label: Raycast Color Palette
nodes.rationale: Near-black blue-tinted background (#07080a), not pure black, creates the feel of a native macOS application rather than a website; Raycast Red is used sparingly as punctuation, not a dominant color.

nodes.label: Inter (with OpenType Features)
nodes.rationale: Used everywhere with extensive OpenType features (calt, kern, liga, ss03) and unusual positive letter-spacing (+0.2px to +0.4px) on a dark background to keep text airy and readable.

nodes.label: macOS-Native Layered Shadow System
nodes.rationale: Multi-layer box-shadows with inset highlights simulate physical depth (glass/brushed metal) rather than flat rectangles, borrowed from macOS window chrome to reinforce the desktop-utility feel.

nodes.label: Renault Color Palette
nodes.rationale: Disciplined black-and-white CTA framework contrasted with vivid aurora-gradient hero photography and sparing Renault Yellow (#EFDF00) reserved for the single highest-priority CTA per screen.

nodes.label: NouvelR (Proprietary Typeface)
nodes.rationale: Designed by Black[Foundry] exclusively for Renault's rebrand; its 'radical r' has a 28-degree terminal cut echoing the diamond logo's angles, and the single family scales from 56px headlines to 8.5px legal text.

nodes.label: PromoCard Light/Dark Chessboard Alternation
nodes.rationale: White editorial panels alternate with black is-alternative-mode sections to create a chessboard-like visual cadence; electrification (E-Tech) content lives in darkness while tradition lives in light.

nodes.label: Aeonik Pro (Display Typeface)
nodes.rationale: Geometric grotesque used at 136px weight 500 with aggressive negative tracking (-2.72px) to create billboard-scale fintech headlines that convey authority through size rather than boldness.

nodes.label: Revolut Color Palette
nodes.rationale: Marketing surface is deliberately restrained to near-black (#191c1f) and white, reserving the comprehensive --rui-* semantic color tokens (danger, warning, teal, blue, etc.) for the product interface rather than marketing pages.

nodes.label: Universal Pill Button System
nodes.rationale: Every button (primary, secondary, outlined, ghost) uses 9999px radius with generous padding (14px 32-34px) and zero shadows, so depth comes entirely from dark/light section contrast.

nodes.label: Sentry Color Palette
nodes.rationale: Warm purple-black backgrounds (#1f1633, #150f23) replace the typical cool grays of developer tools, paired with a lime-green accent (#c2ef4e) used sparingly for high-visibility CTAs against an otherwise warm-dark palette.

nodes.label: Dammit Sans (Brand Display Typeface)
nodes.rationale: Used only at hero scale (88px, weight 700) to carry Sentry's irreverent brand voice ('Code breaks. Fix it faster.'), while Rubik handles all functional UI text as the workhorse font.

nodes.label: Inset Tactile Button Shadow System
nodes.rationale: Primary buttons use inset shadows (rgba(0,0,0,0.1) 0px 1px 3px inset) so they feel pressed INTO the surface, combined with a deep-purple ambient glow that makes content appear to emit its own bioluminescent light.

nodes.label: Ghost Button Component
nodes.rationale: Sole interactive element on the site; kept barely visible (rgba 0.1 fill) so it floats over photography like a heads-up display without competing with imagery.

nodes.label: Universal Sans (Display/Text) Font Family
nodes.rationale: Replaced Gotham to unify the website, mobile app, and in-car software into a single typographic voice across Tesla's whole digital ecosystem.

nodes.label: SpaceX Design System
nodes.rationale: Radical minimalism: full-viewport cinematic photography with an invisible interface (no shadows/cards/borders) so that aerospace photography carries all emotional weight.

nodes.label: Tesla Design System
nodes.rationale: Radical subtraction: the product photography is everything and the interface is designed to be almost nothing, avoiding shadows/gradients so nothing competes with the vehicles.

nodes.label: Design System Inspired by Pacman
nodes.rationale: Retro arcade-inspired design with pixel fonts, dotted borders, playful high-contrast colors, and 8-bit game aesthetics; intent is to keep outputs recognizable to the style family while preserving usability and readability.

nodes.label: Pacman Color Palette
nodes.rationale: Primary token #2A3FE5 favored for CTA emphasis; surface/text tokens kept for legibility. Retro arcade-inspired design with pixel fonts, dotted borders, playful high-contrast colors, and 8-bit game aesthetics; intent is to keep outputs recognizable to the style family while preserving usability and readability.

nodes.label: Pacman Typography System
nodes.rationale: Families: Press Start 2P (primary/display), Space Mono (mono). Headings carry style personality; body text optimizes scanability and contrast.

nodes.label: Design System Inspired by Paper
nodes.rationale: Paper-textured, print-inspired design with minimal colors, clean serif/sans typography, and tactile surface qualities; intent is usability-preserving recognizability.

nodes.label: Design System Inspired by Perspective

nodes.rationale: Straightforward, no-frills design with clean typography, neutral colors, and intuitive layouts that stay out of the way.

nodes.label: Four-Tier Green Brand System
nodes.rationale: Deliberately avoids a single flat brand green; each of the four greens (Starbucks/Accent/House/Uplift) is mapped to a distinct surface role so the brand doesn't flatten.

nodes.label: Frap Floating Circular Order Button
nodes.rationale: The product's signature elevation move: a persistent floating circular CTA with a layered shadow stack, giving the strongest depth cue in an otherwise whisper-soft shadow system.

nodes.label: Starbucks Design System
nodes.rationale: Warm-neutral canvas and calibrated green tiers reference actual café materials, giving a 'warm confident retail flagship' feel rather than a cold tech palette.

nodes.label: Blue-Tinted Multi-Layer Shadow System
nodes.rationale: Uses rgba(50,50,93,0.25) instead of neutral gray/black shadows so that even elevation feels brand-colored, echoing the navy-purple palette; layering a branded far-shadow with a neutral near-shadow creates parallax-like depth.

nodes.label: OpenType ss01 Stylistic Set
nodes.rationale: Non-negotiable across all sohne-var text; the alternate glyph shapes are what define Stripe's geometric, contemporary letterform identity.

nodes.label: Stripe Design System
nodes.rationale: Aims to feel simultaneously technical and luxurious; weight-300 headlines communicate confidence without needing boldness, positioning Stripe as the fintech design gold standard.

nodes.label: Design System Inspired by Figma
nodes.rationale: Interface chrome is kept strictly black-and-white so that colorful product content and screenshots read as the hero visual; the variable font's unusual weight stops (320-540) create hierarchy through micro-differences rather than blunt weight jumps.

nodes.label: Mysteria Purple
nodes.rationale: Named to straddle blue and purple with deliberate ambiguity, used as a singular dramatic hero-gradient gesture against an otherwise white canvas.

nodes.label: Super Sans VF Variable Font
nodes.rationale: Non-standard weight stops (460, 540, 600, 700) deliberately sit between conventional categories, creating a subtly 'off' but confident typographic texture.

nodes.label: Superhuman Design System
nodes.rationale: 'Maximum confidence through minimum decoration' — a productivity tool marketed like a luxury brand, where every pixel must earn its place.

nodes.label: Together AI Design System
nodes.rationale: Pastel-gradient dreamscape intended to make GPU clusters and model inference feel light, airy, and optimistic; splits into a bright 'business' light side and a dark midnight-blue 'research' side.

nodes.label: Warm Editorial Design System
nodes.rationale: A serif-led magazine aesthetic meant to feel like 'a New Yorker interview column online'; chrome (borders, shadows) is treated as subtractive, whitespace and typography lead.

nodes.label: Matter Typeface
nodes.rationale: An unusual choice for a developer tool — its geometric softness signals the terminal is approachable rather than only for 'greybeards'.

nodes.label: Warp Design System
nodes.rationale: 'Restraint through warmth' — rejects the cold blue-tinted blacks typical of developer tools in favor of an earthy near-black and cream text, signaling the terminal is for everyone.

nodes.label: Carbon Design System
nodes.rationale: Token-driven architecture (--cds-* variables) with 0px border-radius and background-color layering instead of shadows communicates enterprise stability and enables systematic theme-switching at the variable level.

nodes.label: Design System Inspired by HashiCorp
nodes.rationale: Dual light/dark mode split mirrors the 'build in light, deploy in dark' developer workflow; per-product brand colors (Terraform purple, Vault yellow, Waypoint teal, Vagrant blue) let each child product retain a distinct identity within the monochrome parent brand.

nodes.label: Design System Inspired by Hugging Face
nodes.norm_label: design system inspired by hugging face

nodes.label: PlayStation Color Palette
nodes.rationale: Three-surface channel layout (near-black hero, paper-white content, cobalt-blue footer); PlayStation Blue is the immovable brand anchor while Cyan is reserved exclusively for interaction states.

nodes.label: Cyan Hover + Scale(1.2) Signature
nodes.rationale: Every primary button fills to cyan, gains a white border and blue outer ring, and scales 1.2x on hover -- a unique 'power-on' animation repeated across the page as PlayStation's interaction signature.

nodes.label: SST (Sony Proprietary Typeface)
nodes.rationale: Sony's custom typeface used at weight 300 for headlines to create a 'quiet authority' voice that lets product photography lead, the opposite of bold, shouting display type.

nodes.label: Resend Color Palette
nodes.rationale: Pure black (#000000) canvas treats email infrastructure like a luxury product; icy blue-tinted frost borders (rgba(214,235,253,0.19)) substitute for shadows, which would be invisible on true black.

nodes.label: Domaine Display (Klim Type Foundry)
nodes.rationale: A serif used at 96px for hero headlines with tight line-height and negative tracking to create magazine-cover-like display text, paired with ABC Favorit for sections and Inter for body in a strict three-font hierarchy.

nodes.label: Frost Border Depth System
nodes.rationale: Because traditional shadows are invisible on pure black, Resend creates depth entirely through icy blue-tinted borders (rgba(214,235,253,0.19)) acting as a 'glass panel floating in space' aesthetic.

nodes.label: Sanity Color Palette
nodes.rationale: A pure achromatic gray scale (#0b0b0b to #ffffff) with no warm or cool bias provides disciplined neutrality against which vivid accent punctuation (neon green, electric blue #0052ef, coral-red #f36458) reads as signal lights in a dark control room.

nodes.label: Colorimetric Depth System
nodes.rationale: Elevation is communicated almost entirely through surface-color shifts (#0b0b0b -> #212121 -> #353535 -> #ffffff) rather than drop shadows, since traditional shadows are native to light interfaces and would be ineffective on dark surfaces; paired with a universal electric-blue hover across all interactive elements.

nodes.label: waldenburgNormal (Display/Body Typeface)
nodes.rationale: A single custom typeface used across editorial display and functional UI with extreme negative tracking at scale (-4.48px at 112px), giving headlines a precision-engineered, machined quality.

nodes.label: Replicate Color Palette
nodes.rationale: High-contrast black (#202020) and white palette punctuated by an explosive orange-red-magenta hero gradient (#ea2804 anchor), signaling a developer playground with festival-poster energy.

nodes.label: rb-freigeist-neue (Display Typeface)
nodes.rationale: Thick, heavy custom display face used up to 128px for the closing manifesto, paired with basier-square for body -- an extreme weight contrast intended to feel like shouting with joy.

nodes.label: Universal Pill Geometry (9999px Radius)
nodes.rationale: 9999px radius is the ONLY border-radius in the system, applied to every button, image, badge, and container -- the most extreme pill-radius commitment cited among major tech brands.

nodes.label: abcNormal (Universal Typeface)
nodes.rationale: A single geometric sans-serif handles every text role from 48px display to 11px micro tags, achieving variety through size, weight, case, and letter-spacing rather than font switching.

nodes.label: Cinematic Full-Bleed Photography as UI
nodes.rationale: Full-bleed AI-generated and AI-enhanced imagery IS the primary UI element rather than icons or diagrams; the interface retreats into near-invisibility (minimal borders, zero shadows) so photography dominates.

nodes.label: Runway Color Palette
nodes.rationale: The interface is intentionally colorless -- dark-dominant with cool-toned neutrals (#767d88, #7d848e) and zero shadows -- so that AI-generated cinematic photography supplies all color and visual richness.

nodes.label: Shopify Color Palette
nodes.rationale: Dark-first design with deep forest-teal undertones (not pure black) stages commerce like a cinematic premiere; Neon Green (#36F4A4) is reserved exclusively for focus rings and small high-energy accents.

nodes.label: NeueHaasGrotesk (Ultralight Display)
nodes.rationale: A refined Helvetica descendant used at monumental scale (96px) but impossibly light weight (330-400) so headlines appear etched in light rather than printed in ink -- the opposite of the bold-display approach most SaaS sites take.

nodes.label: Ultralight Display Typography at Monumental Scale
nodes.norm_label: ultralight display typography at monumental scale
nodes.rationale: Featherweight (330-400) display type at 96px creates a paradox of enormous size and delicate stroke, intended to make commerce technology feel like a science-fiction keynote reveal rather than a SaaS pitch.

nodes.label: HSL-Based Color Token System
nodes.rationale: Using HSL with alpha channels (rather than flat hex) enables translucent layering so colors interact and create depth from minimal color ingredients.

nodes.label: Geist Sans Typeface
nodes.rationale: Extreme negative letter-spacing at display sizes (-2.4px to -2.88px) makes headlines feel 'minified', like code optimized for production.

nodes.label: Shadow-as-Border Technique
nodes.rationale: A zero-offset, zero-blur, 1px-spread box-shadow replaces traditional CSS borders, enabling smoother transitions and rounded corners without box-model clipping issues.

nodes.label: Emerald Signal Green
nodes.rationale: Used with surgical precision as a 'power-on' indicator, glowing from headlines/borders like a circuit board carrying a signal; never used as a surface fill.

nodes.label: System-UI Font Stack (Headings)
nodes.rationale: Chosen for headings so the largest text renders instantly with no FOIT/FOUT, accepting OS-native font variability as a feature rather than a bug.

nodes.label: Supabase Design System
nodes.rationale: Dark-mode-native developer platform aesthetic channeling a premium code editor; deliberately avoids shadows since they're nearly invisible on dark backgrounds, relying on border-color hierarchy instead.

nodes.label: Vercel Design System
nodes.rationale: 'Gallery emptiness': developer infrastructure made invisible through minimalism treated as engineering principle, stripping unnecessary tokens like a compiler.

nodes.label: VoltAgent Design System
nodes.rationale: A 'deep-space command terminal for the AI age' — near-pure-black surfaces broken only by an electric emerald signal, evoking a high-powered IDE at 2am.

nodes.label: FerrariSans (typeface)
nodes.rationale: Proprietary typeface exclusive to Ferrari; compact proportions and medium-weight default (500) are used to convey engineering precision and cannot be substituted without losing brand recognition.

nodes.label: LamboType (typeface)
nodes.rationale: Custom Neo-Grotesk typeface created by Character Type and design agency Strichpunkt; its 12-degree angled terminals are inspired by the aerodynamic lines of Lamborghini's super sports cars, and its hexagonal construction echoes brand geometry throughout the UI (pause button, icon system).

nodes.label: GT Walsheim (typeface)
nodes.rationale: Extreme negative letter-spacing (-5.5px at 110px) at weight 500 only is used to create compressed, kinetic, 'spring-loaded' headlines without ever appearing aggressive (bold is avoided).

nodes.label: Design System Inspired by Linear
nodes.rationale: Dark background is treated as the native medium rather than a theme variant; elevation is communicated via incremental white-opacity steps (luminance stacking, 0.02 to 0.05) rather than shadows, since dark-on-dark drop shadows are nearly invisible.

nodes.label: Ink Blue (#1B365D) accent color
nodes.rationale: Deliberately restricted to <=5% of document surface area; more usage turns the accent into ornament and collapses the print-like restraint that defines the kami system.

nodes.label: Spotify Green Accent Color
nodes.rationale: Used only functionally (play controls, active states, CTAs), never decoratively, to keep the UI achromatic so album art supplies color.

nodes.label: Spotify Design System
nodes.rationale: "Content-first darkness": near-black UI recedes into shadow so album art and content become the primary source of color.

nodes.label: Uber Design System
nodes.rationale: Confident minimalism via a black-and-white duality with virtually no mid-tone grays — the deliberate restraint of a brand established enough to whisper.

nodes.label: Manuka Display Typeface
nodes.rationale: Reserved strictly for display (>=60px) to 'shout the brand'; never used in UI, so the brand identity is loud only where it should be.

nodes.label: StoryStream Timeline Component
nodes.rationale: Stories stack on a dashed vertical rule like commits in a git log rather than floating on a traditional magazine grid — the site's most distinctive layout invention.

nodes.label: Red Divider Band Component
nodes.rationale: A full-width red band with no text or controls that functions purely as a 'new chapter' signal between the hero and the editorial body beneath it.

nodes.label: Vodafone Red
nodes.rationale: The brand's single non-negotiable signature color; must never be substituted or tinted since it constitutes the identity itself.

nodes.label: The Verge Design System
nodes.rationale: 'Condé Nast magazine wired to a chiptune soundboard' — hazard-tape accent colors and a rave-flyer tile aesthetic on a near-black canvas so mint/ultraviolet read as functional signal, never decorative wash.

nodes.label: Vodafone Design System
nodes.rationale: A restrained editorial layout trusts a single fiercely-owned brand red to do the emotional heavy lifting so the rest of the system (near-zero shadow/gradient) can get out of the way.

links.note: Both commit to a universal pill radius (9999px) as the dominant or exclusive interactive-element geometry.
Both apply one universal accent color (PlayStation Cyan / Sanity Electric Blue) consistently to ALL interactive hover/focus states, never as a resting color, as the sole activation signal.
Both are dark-first designs that use theatrical whitespace and let full-bleed cinematic photography/ultralight typography carry visual richness instead of decorative color.
Both use near-black/pure-black canvases with pill-shaped primary CTAs and reject traditional drop shadows in favor of border- or color-based depth mechanisms.
